title: Diagnosing YAML and Configuration Errors knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Diagnosing YAML and Configuration Errors?
options: Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
YAML/configuration failures often come from indentation, invalid fields, wrong types, unsupported inputs, or malformed expressions; validate before debugging runtime.
questions.answer_key: YAML/configuration failures often come from indentation, invalid fields, wrong types, unsupported inputs, or malformed expressions; validate before debugging runtime.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of diagnosing yaml and configuration errors: YAML/configuration failures often come from indentation, invalid fields, wrong types, unsupported inputs, or malformed expressions; validate before debugging runtime. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: A team is working with “Incorrect indentation”. Which practice best fits this topic?
options: Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
YAML is indentation-sensitive. Check that nested values are aligned, values have the expected type, special strings are quoted when needed, and the workflow schema accepts the key at that level.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
questions.answer_key: YAML is indentation-sensitive. Check that nested values are aligned, values have the expected type, special strings are quoted when needed, and the workflow schema accepts the key at that level.
questions.explanation: Incorrect indentation: YAML is indentation-sensitive. Check that nested values are aligned, values have the expected type, special strings are quoted when needed, and the workflow schema accepts the key at that level. Apply the guidance to the actual event, runner, permissions, or artifact boundary and test the relevant case.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to diagnosing yaml and configuration errors?
options: Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: YAML/configuration failures often come from indentation, invalid fields, wrong types, unsupported inputs, or malformed expressions; validate before debugging runtime. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
